briefings.title: Bill Ackman on the worst position in his portfolio and why he is still holding it

people.name: Bill Ackman
people.role: Founder and CEO, Pershing Square Capital Management

briefings.tldr: Bill Ackman identifies Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac as his portfolio's worst-performing yet highest-upside position, while explaining why dominant cash-generating compounders like Microsoft and Netflix remain core holdings despite recent market turbulence.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Bill Ackman identifies Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac as his portfolio's worst-performing yet highest-upside position, while explaining why dominant cash-generating compounders like Microsoft and Netflix remain core holdings despite recent market turbulence.

## Market Sanity & Investment Philosophy
* **Return to Market Sanity:** **Shift Toward Fundamentals:** Bill Ackman notes markets are pivoting back toward cash flows and business quality rather than short-term momentum.
    * **Shiny Objects vs. Quality:** Disruption-focused AI plays and "Neo Clouds" have been treated as speculative shiny objects, leading to discounted valuations for high-quality, dominant compounders.
    * **Deployment Pace:** Pershing Square has made seven new investments in the past six months, taking advantage of compressed valuations on long-desired companies.
* **Macro & Valuation Outlook:** **Balanced S&P 500:** Ackman views the overall stock market as reasonably valued with strong earnings growth, declining to make short-term predictions on the Nasdaq.
    * **Compute as an Asset:** He is a believer in owning compute over time, provided it is held in a non-leveraged format and tied to defensible business models.

## Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and High-Upside Special Situations
* **Contrarian High-Conviction Bet:** **Worst Position with Highest Upside:** Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac represent Pershing Square's worst-performing position down over 60% this calendar year (costing 800-900 basis points of performance), yet Ackman views them as $4 stocks with a true value of $40 to $50.
    * **13-Year Holding Period:** Pershing Square has held the stocks for 13 years betting on release from conservatorship and privatization.
    * **Political Catalysts:** The thesis rests on presidential action—noting prior positive movement during Trump's term, a commitment letter from 2021, and recent comments by Howard Lutnick indicating potential movement.
    * **Asymmetric Risk-Reward:** Midterm political shifts handicap broad economic policy but leave Fannie and Freddie as a prime executive-action opportunity. Treasury Secretary comments suggest addressing the companies in the back half of the term.

## Big Tech, AI Infrastructure, and Software Defensibility
* **Microsoft Enterprise Moat:** **Enterprise Stickiness:** Microsoft remains a strong core holding due to its embedded position across 450 million business seats, robust cybersecurity, and centralized control over corporate AI usage.
    * **Hyper scaler Gateways:** Anthropic routes nearly 50% of its revenues through hyperscalers like Amazon and Microsoft, proving that distribution channels remain vital.
* **Netflix Valuation & Prospects:** **Compelling Valuation:** Netflix trades at 16x to 17x earnings (down from mid-30s), representing a significant discount from its highs despite strong subscription growth and renewals.
    * **Growth Drivers:** Catalysts for next year include passage of time, continued earnings and revenue growth, content wins, and improved subscriber disclosure.
* **NVIDIA & Jensen Huang:** **Character Defense:** Bill Ackman publicly defended NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, citing personal experience with Huang's help on a medical project for Ackman's daughter and advocating an "innocent until proven guilty" stance.
    * **Founder Succession:** While acknowledging Huang is an irreplaceable founder-led visionary akin to Steve Jobs, Ackman believes NVIDIA remains well-positioned for the long term.

## Why Anthropic Does Not Fit the Portfolio
* **High-Capital Risk Profile:** **Complex Financial Modeling:** While Ackman calls Anthropic perhaps the most amazing business story of the century, its requirement for massive capital investments makes valuation and future cash flows difficult to nail down with precision.
    * **Speculative Bet:** Unlike a widget company or Visa, companies requiring continuous massive capital outlays carry a higher risk if revenue acceleration misses projections or capital access tightens.
    * **Operating Profitability:** While Anthropic approaches operating profitability, its long-term business model depends heavily on maintaining a leading position in compute and AI capabilities.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Bill Ackman predicts** that if the president follows through on previous commitments regarding Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, they will become $40 to $50 stocks from their current $4 level.
* **Bill Ackman predicts** the Treasury will address the conservatorship of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in the back half of the presidential term rather than prior to the midterms.

## Notable Quotes
> "The worst-performing position is also the one I think has the most upside: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which our firm has held for 13 years on a bet they are released from conservatorship." — **Bill Ackman**

> "Anytime you have a business that requires a massive investment in order to continue to accelerate its growth... it's a higher risk proposition. We're kind of we think of ourselves as very low-risk investors." — **Bill Ackman**

> "If you're the gateway to how people interacts with the basic workflows of a desk worker... which is what Microsoft is today, I think it's a much more difficult position to dislodge." — **Bill Ackman**

briefings.title: Cyberattacks Used to Take Months. AI Can Do It in Minutes.
briefings.tldr: AI is collapsing the timeline for cyberattacks from months to just 20 minutes, marking the beginning of "Black October"—a wave of unprecedented, agentic attacks where AI-driven offensive capabilities are outperforming human hackers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI is collapsing the timeline for cyberattacks from months to just 20 minutes, marking the beginning of "Black October"—a wave of unprecedented, agentic attacks where AI-driven offensive capabilities are outperforming human hackers.

## The AI Offensive Surge and "Black October"
* **The Definition of Black October:** Ami Luttwak characterizes October as a black swan event and a turning point for cybersecurity, citing an unprecedented volume and severity of vulnerabilities combined with new AI-powered speed and expertise.
* **Collapsed Exploit Timelines:** AI has compressed the time required to write complex exploits from weeks or months down to roughly 20 minutes.
* **The Open-Source Threat Multiplier:** While proprietary frontier models advanced vulnerability discovery months ago, open-source models have now caught up, placing sophisticated offensive capabilities into a much wider set of hands.
* **Real-World Impact on Startups:** 
  * AI development platforms are being specifically targeted because they hold valuable AI credentials and API keys.
  * Startups are a prime target for LLM-driven attacks, facing threats that can steal keys and drain accounts within minutes.
* **Case Study: PHP2Shell:** 
  * Affecting a technology running on roughly 70% of the internet, PHP2Shell impacted nearly 100% of Wiz's customer base.
  * While 50% of customers patched within the first 2 to 3 days, complete industry-wide resolution will take years due to unpatchable older versions and delayed Linux distribution updates.
* **AI vs. Human Capability:** Ami Luttwak notes that cybersecurity is almost the only domain where AI is now demonstrably better than humans, executing complex zero-day attacks (such as on kernel drivers) at a frequency never before possible.

## Defensive Strategies: Pipelines, Automation, and Red Agents
* **The New Engineering Challenge:** Developing secure AI systems requires managing costs via intelligent, multi-tiered pipelines rather than running expensive frontier models on every single event.
  * **Blue Agent Pipeline:** Starts with deterministic detection, moves through cheap model detection, escalates to advanced models, and finally uses the most advanced model to confirm maliciousness before alerting the customer.
  * **Red Agent Pipeline:** Begins with deterministic exposure analysis, followed by an exposure agent looking at unauthenticated internet-facing endpoints, and scales up to deep pentests and code analysis for critical applications.
* **Continuous Testing vs. Static Scanning:** Static scans (like early Mitos scans) can waste millions of dollars without providing continuous protection. Security must shift to a continuous, intelligent model that balances internal code analysis, disk scans, and runtime monitoring.
* **Prioritizing External Exposure:** Ami Luttwak emphasizes that scanning unauthenticated external attack surfaces (such as hardcoded keys in mobile apps) is far more urgent and effective than immediately diving into code scanning.
* **Automated Remediation Constraints:** While new startups can build automated CI/CD and agentic dev-to-patch pipelines from day one, legacy companies face massive hurdles due to obscure organizational knowledge and legacy codebases.

## Security Budgets, Architecture, and Industry Transformation
* **Security vs. Compliance Work:** Ami Luttwak argues that most of what traditional security teams do is not actual security; true security focuses on proactive preparation (red teaming and guardrails), critical risk mitigation, and response readiness.
* **The Limitations of Budgets:** Increasing security budgets and buying traditional tools (like classic CSPM configuration check lists) will not solve the modern crisis. The real solution requires fundamental **secure architecture**—sandboxing, isolation, network lockdown, and process lockdown.
* **Obsolescence of Legacy Stack:** CISOs are using the current crisis to reboot their security vendor stacks, phasing out legacy tools in favor of AI-native technologies built for modern cloud and AI threats.
* **Public Infrastructure Risks:** Beyond tech enterprises, real-world legacy infrastructure—such as refrigeration units and public services—is connected to the internet and acutely vulnerable to mass-scale disruption. In response, Wiz launched **Scan for Good** to help public services and nonprofits identify exposures.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Ami Luttwak predicts** that the only companies able to survive the next several years will be those that actively build security automation, conduct continuous security reviews, and redesign their internet-exposed systems for zero-trust environments.
* **Zane Lackey predicts** that the industry is returning to an era reminiscent of the 1990s and 2000s, characterized by persistent unauthenticated zero-days, frequent breaches, and the potential resurgence of internet worms similar to the Windows XP days.

## Notable Quotes
> "We are calling this Black October... since it's a black swan event. We've never seen, never ever seen so many security incidents happen in a single month."
> — **Ami Luttwak**

> "Most of what security teams do is not security... security in my view is getting either ready for the attacker attacking yourself or putting guardrails for the attack when it comes."
> — **Ami Luttwak**

> "We are at an era where AI is better than humans. I think the only companies that will be able to survive are companies that are building now not just security automation, security design, security reviews."
> — **Ami Luttwak**

briefings.title: How Mozilla uses GPT-6 Cyber to find and fix Firefox vulnerabilities
briefings.tldr: By combining decades of browser security preparation with GPT-6 Cyber agents, Mozilla scaled its bug discovery and fix rate by 8× from 2025 to 2026, successfully preventing any successful exploits at the annual Pwn2Own competition.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
By combining decades of browser security preparation with GPT-6 Cyber agents, Mozilla scaled its bug discovery and fix rate by 8× from 2025 to 2026, successfully preventing any successful exploits at the annual Pwn2Own competition.

## 1. Pwn2Own Fire Drill and Agentic Partnerships
* **Pre-Competition Scramble:** Browsers remain a top target for the annual Pwn2Own hacking competition, which Mozilla uses as a real-world fire drill.
  * **OpenAI Collaboration:** Shortly before the 2026 event, the OpenAI cyber team filed a few bugs; after Mozilla quickly fixed and uplifted them, it was discovered that a number of researcher submissions were attempting to use those exact bugs.
  * **Event Outcome:** Mozilla successfully defended Firefox, with no participants able to compromise the browser.

## 2. Decades of Foundational Security Preparation
* **Prerequisites for AI Integration:** Mozilla’s ability to successfully adopt an agentic tool chain was built on years of foundational security investments.
  * **External Bug Bounties:** Decades of running an external bug bounty program established comfort with receiving a high volume of external reports.
  * **Internal Tooling:** Long-standing adoption of address sanitizers, fuzzers, debuggable builds, and internal red teams provided the exact primitives agents now use to spin up Firefox instances, test potential exploits, and iterate rapidly.

## 3. Agentic Security Pipeline & Inner Loop Architecture
* **Intelligent File Prioritization:** Alphabetical file-tree scanning proved ineffective, leading Mozilla to use an LLM-based grading system incorporating technical documentation, researcher artifacts, and historical risk scores to generate target lists.
* **Inner Loop Execution:** 
  * **VM Isolation & Goals:** An agent is placed inside its own VM with access to the Firefox source code and fuzzing tool chain, tasked with finding bugs via static analysis, custom mini-fuzzers, and dynamic testing.
  * **Deterministic Verification:** The agent must produce deterministic proof (such as an HTML file causing a crash in Firefox) to exit the inner loop.
* **Secondary Judging & Quality Control:** 
  * A second grading agent checks the work to catch anomalies (such as an agent artificially patching the codebase to force a crash) and grade severity against Mozilla's threat model, resulting in a tiny false positive rate.
  * **Auto-Fix Generation:** Within the inner loop, an agent generates a code patch and a test case to accompany the bug report.

## 4. Scaling Triage, Deduplication, and Variant Analysis
* **Automated Deduplication Challenges:** Distinguishing unique vulnerabilities from hundreds of scan findings proved unintuitively difficult due to nuanced crash stack variations.
  * **Database Ingestion:** Mozilla ingests all findings into a local database and tasks an agent with connecting dots under strict guidance.
  * **False Duplicate Safeguards:** If a finding is marked as a duplicate, the system creates a reminder to confirm it no longer works once the primary bug lands in the tree.
* **Severity Re-Evaluation via GPT-6 Cyber:** Powerful cyber models uncovered that certain bugs originally graded as moderate/low severity actually bypassed architectural hardening and qualified as security-high, providing vital feedback to improve defense-in-depth.
* **Broad Variant and Commit Scanning:** 
  * **Variant Analysis:** Bundling known security bugs fixed in 2025 and tasking agents to hunt for similar patterns across the codebase yielded a majority of findings by September, generating fewer duplicate reports.
  * **Commit Scanning:** Narrowly inspecting new commits for potential vulnerabilities works alongside broad variant scans as part of the core strategy.

## 5. Engineer Workflows and 8× Metric Scaling
* **Assisting Human Engineers:** While generated fix patches are rarely landable as-is due to narrow targeting or missing codebase context, expert browser engineers use them alongside descriptions and evidence to review and land fixes.
* **Massive Productivity Gains:** Across its security workflow, Mozilla achieved an **8× increase in bug discovery and fixes** from **2025 to 2026**.
* **Agentic Vulnerability Workbench:** 
  * **SQLite Ingestion:** Signals from all runs, bugs, and engineer comments are ingested into a local SQLite file on red team engineers' machines.
  * **Workflow Queries:** Coding agents can run SQL queries to plan next scanning patches based on Slack hints or review raw traces and `blockers.yaml` files to fix environment dependencies.

## Notable Quotes
> "Different models find different bugs even if you've scanned the code multiple times."
> — Brian Grinstead

> "Every bug that we fix is gone... We want to have zero bugs, and that's sort of the the guiding light out towards the future."
> — Brian Grinstead

briefings.title: Recursive self-improvement has started
briefings.tldr: AI is already accelerating its own R&D, making models that rival the best human researchers globally plausibly as early as 2027—sparking a recursive self-improvement loop that could yield superintelligence within years.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI is already accelerating its own R&D, making models that rival the best human researchers globally plausibly as early as 2027—sparking a recursive self-improvement loop that could yield superintelligence within years.

## AI Research Acceleration & The Mathematics Parallel
* **Current Acceleration at Frontiers:** Independent evaluation organizations and frontier labs report dramatic internal speedups driven by AI use.
    * **Meter's Assessment:** Found Anthropic's rate of AI progress on well-scoped tasks doubled over a year, with the "majority of this acceleration" attributable to AI-driven R&D.
    * **OpenAI & Anthropic Metrics:** OpenAI reported that its heaviest 10% of users scaled internal coding agent spending from $1,000/day to over $7,000/day between early summer and August; Anthropic reported Claude leading 26% of its AI R&D work by September (up from <1% in February).
* **Explosive Progress in Mathematics:** AI models have sliced through verifiable math domains, turning complex open problems into routine side quests.
    * **Timeline of Capability:** Models advanced from failing high school math competitions in 2024 to winning IMO gold medals in 2025, and ultimately solving a Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours.
    * **Verifiability Advantage:** While math progress focuses heavily on verification (e.g., finding counterexamples) rather than broad theory, AI labs prioritize empirical algorithmic recipes over theory, making AI research a natural fit for this capability.
* **The Transformer Analogy:** Breakthroughs like the Transformer architecture—built on known components like attention and residual networks—represent the exact type of systematic idea-matching and small-scale experimentation at which AI models excel.

## Dynamics of the Intelligence Explosion
* **Three Drivers of Algorithmic Speedup:** Once AIs match human AI researchers, progress will surge due to speed, intelligence, and scale.
    * **Speed:** Current AIs operate at 10x human speed around the clock, allowing individual automated researchers to complete roughly 50x more work per calendar week than a human.
    * **Intelligence:** Every automated researcher will match the caliber of the top 50 foundational researchers who typically drive 80% of algorithmic progress at a frontier lab.
    * **Scale:** Unlike tasks requiring a singular voice (like writing a novel), AI research features modular subtasks and verifiable proxies, enabling massive parallelization (swarms trying thousands of approaches simultaneously).
* **Two Divergent Takeoff Scenarios:** The net trajectory depends on whether recursive self-improvement outpaces the increasing difficulty of finding new ideas.
    * **Software-Only Singularity (50% probability):** AIs rapidly iterate smarter versions of themselves within months, scraping against physical hardware limits.
    * **The Spark (50% probability):** Achieves 3 to 6 years of progress in a single calendar year before stabilizing while humanity builds more compute.

## Real-World Generalization & Data Ownership
* **Scaling RL for General Skills:** While data centers cannot directly simulate real-world environments like courtroom litigation or business founding, massive reinforcement learning (RL) in hyper-realistic virtual worlds will forge general-purpose learners.
    * **Virtual Training Environments:** AIs will navigate complex, multi-century corporate competition simulations, historical back-tests (e.g., predicting the Cuban Missile Crisis or deriving General Relativity from pre-1700 data), and algorithmic self-improvement.
    * **Evolutionary Precedent:** Natural evolution built a general-purpose human learner using a crude verifier (survival/reproduction) on the savanna; deliberate RL optimization will yield far superior transfer capabilities.
* **Rapid Deployment Ramp-Up:** Post-spark AIs will bridge the real-world experience gap within months of deployment—mirroring young historical prodigies like 27-year-old Napoleon or 25-year-old Rockefeller—while digesting enterprise data (emails, Slack messages, employee interviews) in days.
* **Synthetic Data Generation:** Data scarcity will be overcome as automated systems construct massive, high-quality synthetic datasets and RL environments using difficulty and correctness as reward signals.

## Verifiable R&D Proxies & Overcoming Objections
* **The Three Buckets of Verifiable AI R&D:** Algorithmic progress is trackable via clear internal metrics across pre-training, post-training, and inference.
    * **Pre-Training:** Minimized compute required to reach fixed pre-training loss on nano-GPT benchmarks, alongside scaling law predictions (e.g., Magic's model matching DeepSeek V4 Pro for half the compute of original GPT-3, roughly $500,000).
    * **Post-Training:** Measured reductions in compute/data/time required for new RL environments, evaluation on unseen tasks (e.g., Bytedance's *Edgebench*), and internal historical replays (e.g., Anthropic's *Coobch* benchmark).
    * **Inference Efficiency:** Directly measurable metrics including GPU utilization, KV cache size per token, total forward-pass flops, and latency.
* **Addressing Key Bottlenecks:**
    * **Continual Learning:** Solved either via extended in-context learning windows or online learning research problems possessing clean verifiable proxies; even amnesiac models can solve Millennium Prize problems without long-term memory.
    * **Research Taste & Proxies:** Paradigm-agnostic outer-loop proxies (e.g., solving millennium problems or discovering physical laws from historical data) bridge paradigm shifts.
    * **Experiment Compute Constraints:** Frontier compute scaling (quadrupling yearly) will provide thousands of agents with sufficient hourly compute to run GPT-3 scale experiments, replacing scarce human researcher time with compute-heavy ablation pipelines.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** We are only a couple of years away—and possibly only a couple of months away—from AIs that are as good as the best humans at AI research.
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** By 2030, and plausibly as early as next year, we will have AIs that are at least as good as the best human experts in every field.
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** The median year for when automated researchers will be as good as the very best human AI researchers at doing AI research is 2028 (assuming full-steam-ahead development without intentional slowdowns or government intervention).
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** There is at least a 25% chance that automating AI-level researchers will not happen until after 2032 due to persistent difficulties like continual learning.
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** There is a real possibility that AI capabilities reach this milestone as early as 2027, supported by straightforward takeoffs models fed by Anthropic's reported doubling of progress rates.
* **Dwarkesh Patel:** There is a 50% probability of a software-only singularity and a 50% probability of a spark scenario (compressing 3 to 6 years of progress into a single calendar year).

## Notable Quotes
> "If you take at face value that AI is now nearly doubling the rate of AI capabilities progress and assume that acceleration from AI is smooth, this naively implies that we would reach extreme super intelligence within a year."
> — *AJ Coocher (cited by Dwarkesh Patel)*

> "And there is one sure thing about the fall of gods: they do not fall a little, they crash and shatter."
> — *Dwarkesh Patel (quoting John Steinbeck's East of Eden regarding math progress)*

> "The gods above must work from the same principles as the ants below."
> — *Anonymous AI Researcher (cited by Dwarkesh Patel)*

briefings.title: SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril & Onodrim | The Return of Conglomerates

people.name: Christian Garrett
people.role: Partner, 137 Ventures and Co-Founder, Onodrim Industries

briefings.tldr: SpaceX has evolved from a launch provider into a dominant AI hyperscaler and vertically integrated conglomerate, while firms like 137 Ventures are investing in multi-product tech giants and co-founding platforms like Onodrim to scale European aerospace and defense manufacturing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
SpaceX has evolved from a launch provider into a dominant AI hyperscaler and vertically integrated conglomerate, while firms like 137 Ventures are investing in multi-product tech giants and co-founding platforms like Onodrim to scale European aerospace and defense manufacturing.

## SpaceX's Evolution: From Launch Provider to AI Hyperscaler
- **Financial and Operational Growth:** 
  - 137 Ventures has invested in SpaceX for 16 years, making it their largest position.
  - SpaceX recently posted top-line growth of ~160%, $4.4 billion in net income, and $8.8 to $9.10 billion of EBITDA in Q3.
  - The business is valued at $2 trillion, trading at roughly 20 to 30 times consensus EBITDA based on Q3 performance.
  - More than 50% of SpaceX's revenue is now attributed to AI in some capacity.
- **Hyperscaler Strategy & Compute Infrastructure:** 
  - SpaceX is building out software, services, and game infrastructure around its compute stack, functioning as a true hyperscaler.
  - Reiterated earnings calls indicate sub-12-month payback periods, signaling massive unsatisfied demand where supply cannot match demand.
  - Vertical integration allows SpaceX to monetize from the app layer and model layer down to compute, providing risk-adjusted investment durability against shifts between open-source and closed-source models.
  - If outer-year demand slows, SpaceX can shift capacity to its own products, making its capex risk nominal and shorter-duration.
- **Starship & Starlink Milestones:** 
  - Starship is successfully flying, delivering payloads to space—including compute payloads on V3 satellites for Starlink.
  - A single launch with a handful of Starlink V3s delivered roughly 1% of the world's capacity, with tens of thousands more planned.
  - Starlink is expanding rapidly into Direct-to-Cell (DDC).
  - Starship is lowering launch costs by orders of magnitude, enabling downstream businesses like Varta (founded by Delian, Will Brewy) to serve pharmaceutical and defense industries.
- **Orbital Data Centers & Space Compute:** 
  - Starcloud (led by CEO Philip in Seattle) is developing Starcloud 2 and early iterations of Starcloud 3 to be hosted on Starship.
  - Orbital compute satellites are targeted for launch in the back half of next year.
  - Orbital data centers solve terrestrial constraints around power, land, and energy.

## Portfolio Strategy: Growth, Valuations, and Power Law Dynamics
- **Long-Term Duration Over Single-Year Rates:** 
  - 137 Ventures focuses on the duration of compounding revenue growth rather than chasing single-year spikes (e.g., SpaceX compounding at ~40% for 20 years).
  - As minority growth-stage investors, the firm wants conviction that a portfolio company can compound for decades.
- **Key Portfolio Investments:** 
  - **Ramp:** Co-founded/invested years ago; consolidating the back-office financial operations stack with significant room for further monetization and product expansion; valued around $60 billion.
  - **Cognition:** Sitting at the harness and app layer; recently valued at $48 billion with rumors of a round reaching $60–$70 billion.
  - **Anduril:** Valued at $90 billion; utilizes a common back-end software/AI infrastructure platform called **Lattice** that powers all products, creating compounding value with every marginal sale.
  - **Hex:** Co-led by 137 Ventures, sitting at the data analytics and workflows layer with Barry.
  - **Applied Intuition:** Transforming the automotive, construction, mining, and trucking industries by selling software and touching electronics/controllers/wiring to improve vehicle cost structures and autonomy.
  - **General Matter:** Re-industrializing uranium enrichment and bringing back critical capacity using modern tools and sensors.
- **Valuation Realities & Power Law:** 
  - Capital flooding into growth stages leads to higher entry prices, but the power law of venture returns heavily compensates for premium pricing on category-defining winners (similar to historical Fintech outcomes like Stripe, Revolute, Ramp, and NuBank).

## The Return of the Conglomerate & Dual-Use Defense
- **Modern vs. Historical Conglomerates:** 
  - Traditional conglomerates of the 1980s suffered from disparate subsidiaries with no shared operating systems or synergies.
  - Modern tech conglomerates (like Apple, SpaceX, and Anduril) utilize a common operating tech platform and vertical integration to manage multiple high-growth business lines.
- **The Dual-Use Imperative:** 
  - True resilience requires "capital C" dual-use conglomerates that sell to both the commercial private sector and government/defense.
  - Palantir and SpaceX are prime examples where the majority of revenue stems from the commercial sector, subsidizing and maintaining surge capacity for the defense sector without relying solely on industrial policy.
  - China's defense primes derive 68% of revenue from the commercial sector, mirroring the commercial dominance needed in the West (e.g., commercial shipping driving naval manufacturing).

## Onodrim Industries: Re-industrializing European Defense
- **Founding & Scale:** 
  - Co-founded by Christian Garrett alongside ISIS and Alex (former early Palantir leaders).
  - Onodrim is an aerospace and defense scale-up platform that recently raised a **$300 million Series A at a $1.3 billion valuation**.
- **The European Bottleneck:** 
  - While thousands of European drone companies and neo-prime startups ("Start Quantum," Cambridge-backed firms) are heavily funded, the critical supplier layer underneath—components, engines, precision manufacturing—is fragmented and under-capitalized.
  - Unlike the US, Europe lacks supplier consolidators like Transdigm, Teledyne, Hico, or Honeywell.
- **Strategy & Execution:** 
  - Onodrim acquires and partners with multigenerational European aerospace, defense, and industrial manufacturers.
  - The platform deploys capital (capex), engineering resources, and modern manufacturing technology (including AI software to modernize operations) to scale these businesses into pan-European and global champions.
  - The team spans 9 nationalities, combining backgrounds from private equity, traditional defense, McKinsey, and tech firms like Palantir and SpaceX.

## Industry Culture, Zero-Sum Mindsets, and Political Weaponization
- **Preserving Non-Zero-Sum Culture:** 
  - Unlike legacy industries, the technology sector has historically thrived on a non-zero-sum, high-growth culture.
  - Petty infighting, internal attacks, and tribalism threaten to erode the collaborative spirit that drives global economic share.
- **The Danger of Political Weaponization:** 
  - Tech companies and founders are increasingly facing political targeting and boycotts based on personal political views.
  - This trend is misguided because these companies are nonpartisan engines of job creation, GDP growth, and national security.
  - Consumer choices should rely on the merits of products and markets, rather than political litmus tests that could severely backfire on Western competitiveness.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Space Compute Launch Timeline:** SpaceX is on track to launch some of the first orbital compute satellites in the **back half of next year** (*Christian Garrett*).
- **Onodrim Milestones:** Onodrim Industries will soon announce its **first set of acquisitions** and key partnerships with leading defense and commercial prime companies (*Christian Garrett*).
- **Hillen Valley Conference Timing:** The next Hillen Valley event will take place in **Spring (March or April)**, depending on the congressional calendar, with dates finalized by late this year or early next year (*Christian Garrett*).

## Notable Quotes
> "The business is honestly just getting started... they grew top line like 160%, they posted $4.4 billion in net income, $8.8 to $9.10 billion of EBITDA... Trading anywhere from 20 to 30 times 2027 [EBITDA] for a $2 trillion company that is dominant provider in multiple critical industries."
> — Christian Garrett

> "You'd much rather own a quality asset that's a 5x and pay a 25% premium to buy it than to own a shitty asset, right, and pay a 25% discount to buy it."
> — Christian Garrett (quoting Teddy Forstmann)

> "To have the type of capacity that we really need from a defense perspective, you're going to need to be dominant in the commercial industry or else it just won't work... Palantir and SpaceX are the only examples of this [dual-use conglomerates]."
> — Christian Garrett

> "If there's a great idea, most times you're not the person to go do it. If it's a weird case where you're the person to go do it, then by all means go and do it."
> — Christian Garrett

briefings.title: The AI Debate is No Longer Boom vs Bust: Why It’s Time to Go Back to Stock Picking | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman argues that the AI trade requires a differential diagnosis with distinct winners and losers following the midterms, Jensen Huang’s resignation, and data center moratorium threats, while the housing market stagnates at a 16-year low.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Steve Eisman argues that the AI trade requires a differential diagnosis with distinct winners and losers following the midterms, Jensen Huang’s resignation, and data center moratorium threats, while the housing market stagnates at a 16-year low.

## AI Market Dynamics & Narrative Shifts
* **Shift in Focus:** The AI narrative has evolved from capex and neocloud debt concerns to political threats following a Democratic sweep of Congress.
* **Data Center Moratoriums:** 
  * Many elections were won on platforms opposing data centers, raising fears that construction will be curtailed or halted nationwide.
  * Eisman notes the irony of tech executives publicly warning that AI is dangerous enough to destroy mankind right before a general election.
* **Market Impact:** The combination of elections, core debt, wobbly Anthropic IPO valuations, and the Jensen Wong drama have sucked trillions of dollars in valuation from the stock market and retirement accounts.
* **The Bull Case (Slower Capex):** A 10% to 30% slowdown in AI data center construction could cause AI capex to peak in 2027 and hyperscalers to return to positive cash flow by as early as the second half of 2027.
* **Treasury Market Relief:** Slower capex would ease the crowding-out effect on US Treasuries caused by $500 billion in AI debt needs expected in 2026, putting downward pressure on long-term interest rates.
* **Local Permitting Strategy:** Cash payments from tech firms to local communities (improving schools, lowering taxes) may successfully overcome local political resistance once spotlights turn down.

## Negative Housing Data & Cost of Living
* **Stagnant Market:** Existing home sales decreased 5.5% to an annualized rate of 3.75 million, hitting a 16-year low.
* **The Lock-In Effect:** Most homeowners refinanced into 3% to 3.5% mortgages during COVID; buying a new home at 7% mortgage rates makes selling economically unviable.
* **Inventory vs. New Listings:** 
  * Active inventory in October hit 183,500 homes in the US, up 7.4% year-over-year (the fastest annual growth rate in almost a year).
  * New listings are falling simultaneously, down 7.5% year-over-year, indicating buyers are refusing to buy at current high prices and sellers are keeping listings private.
* **Escalating Ownership Costs:** Property taxes, property and casualty insurance, permits, and renovation costs are estimated to be at least 50% higher than five years ago.

## Earnings & Company Performance
* **Charter:** 
  * Steve Eisman admitted he was wrong, threw in the towel, and sold his shares after two bad quarters.
  * Revenue was down 1.5%, adjusted EBITDA was down 4%, and broadband customers dropped by a whopping 233,000; the stock is down 44% this year.
* **Meritage (Housing):** With the housing market severely depressed, Eisman threw in the towel on this stock as well.
* **Skydance (Paramount & Warner Bros. combination):** 
  * Q3 revenue reached $7 billion, up 5% year-over-year.
  * Operating income was a meager $368 million (5% margin), and net income was just $73 million, weighed down by unprofitable legacy media.
* **CoreWeave:** 
  * Went public on March 27, 2025 at $39; stock trades at $56 after peaking at $138 in May 2025.
  * The three founders have combined to sell over $3 billion in stock since going public, while buying back zero shares.
  * Nvidia has invested $2 billion in CoreWeave, creating a safety net perception that may weaken under new leadership following Jensen Huang's resignation.
  * Q3 revenue reached $3.7 billion, up 168%, but EPS was a large negative $1.27.
  * Operating cash flow was positive $2 billion against $9.8 billion in investing cash flows (equipment purchases), resulting in a negative free cash flow of $7.8 billion.
  * Total long-term debt and operating lease liabilities hit $54 billion, with debt currently priced at a prohibitive 15%.
* **Nebius:** 
  * Q3 loss was 13 cents (improved from a loss of 40 cents last year); revenue reached $981 million, up over 500%.
  * FY 2026 revenue is expected at the low end of the $3 billion to $3.4 billion range (consensus was $3.35 billion); 2027 revenue is guided to $12 billion to $13 billion.
  * Capex guidance shocked investors: FY 2026 capex raised to $27 billion (from $20B–$25B), and FY 2027 capex projected at $40 billion to $45 billion (well above expectations of $29 billion), causing the stock to fall 19%.
* **Cisco:** 
  * Reported Q1 fiscal 2027 results (fiscal year ends July 31st).
  * EPS of $1.40 was up 40% year-over-year (a beat); revenue of $18.5 billion was up 24% year-over-year (a beat).
  * Raised EPS and fiscal revenue guidance for fiscal 2027, demonstrating strong current picks-and-shovels demand.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Gary Gensler / CFTC / SEC Prediction (via guest interview preview):** Gary Gensler publicly stated that AI infrastructure is being built before sufficient revenues exist to support it, leading to a correction within the next 18 to 30 months.
* **Steve Eisman Housing Prediction:** Melody Wright of Unicus Research predicts housing prices will decline all over the country over the next few years, a trajectory Eisman believes will happen if mortgage rates and ownership costs do not improve.
* **Steve Eisman AI Capex Prediction:** AI data center construction projects will slow down by approximately 10% to 30%, which will cause AI capex to peak in 2027 and hyperscalers to return to positive cash flow by as early as the second half of 2027.

## Notable Quotes
> "The election combined with the coreweave debt, the wobbly foundations of the anthropic IPO valuation, and now the Jensen drama have all sucked trillions of dollars in valuation from the stock market and voters retirement accounts."
> — Steve Eisman

> "It might be just me, but publicly asserting that your technology is so dangerous it can destroy mankind and saying that on the eve of a general election strikes me as amongst the strangest behavior I have ever seen in my entire investing life."
> — Steve Eisman

> "Most fantasy novels are about the hero's journey. Robin Hobb wrote a story about a hero's life."
> — Steve Eisman

briefings.title: "Xia" | A 6-Hour Interview with Soulframe Liang, Producer of Phantom Blade Zero
briefings.tldr: Soulframe Liang, producer of Phantom Blade Zero, discusses his 15-year journey from an indie developer to leading S-GAME, the deep influence of Gu Long's dark wuxia aesthetics on his work, and the evolution of the xia spirit into modern individual self-actualization.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Soulframe Liang, producer of *Phantom Blade Zero*, discusses his 15-year journey from an indie developer to leading S-GAME, the deep influence of Gu Long's dark *wuxia* aesthetics on his work, and the evolution of the *xia* spirit into modern individual self-actualization.

## 1. Defining the *Xia* and Dark *Wuxia* Aesthetics
- **The True Nature of *Xia*:** **Liang Qiwei** explains that a *xia* differs from an ordinary good person by operating under extreme conditions, bearing massive risks, and maintaining human compassion amidst systemic injustice and collapsing order.
- **Grassroots Roots:** **Liang** notes that unlike Western knights who protected feudal lords or Japanese samurai serving shoguns, Chinese *xia* emerge from the margins (*jianghu*) in opposition to the imperial court.
- **The "Pathological" Aesthetic:** Drawing from Gu Long's works (e.g., *Sentimental Swordsman, Ruthless Sword*), **Liang** highlights that *wuxia* characters invariably carry flaws or "pathologies" (e.g., Li Xunhuan’s tuberculosis, Fu Hongxue's lameness), creating an aesthetic collision between extreme beauty and extreme darkness.

## 2. Evolution of *Wuxia* and Modern Values
- **Shift from Self-Sacrifice to Self-Actualization:** **Liang** contrasts classic *wuxia* tropes of self-abnegation for another person with modern values where young people prioritize personal growth, inner peace, and the "power fantasy" of leveling up (*"In hardship, cultivate yourself; in success, better the world"*).
- **The "Wuxia Punk" Paradigm:** **Liang** argues that traditional *wuxia* moves from the self outward to others, whereas modern "wuxia punk" moves from the self back to the self—mirroring the closed-loop growth found in modern web novels and Soulslike games.
- **Rejection of Preachy Tropes:** **Liang** admits early trailers for *Phantom Blade Zero* failed when they pasted on grand, hypocritical slogans like *"The greatest xia serves the nation and the people,"* which players immediately saw through as insincere "self-gilding."

## 3. Liang Qiwei's Entrepreneurial Journey and S-GAME
- **The 2011 Startup Pivot:** After failing an engineering economics course and having his Tsinghua grad school recommendation revoked, **Liang** studied architecture at Yale before returning to China in May 2011 with a backpack and a dream to make games.
- **Early Angel Funding:** **Xu Xiaoping** (ZhenFund) personally wired **Liang** 1,000,000 RMB without a term sheet to start S-GAME in Beijing's Huaqing Jiayuan.
- **The Trap of Capitalization (2015–2017):** **Liang** reflects on the era following *Phantom Blade 1*'s commercial success (pulling in 10 to 20 million RMB monthly with a 20-person team), where he and his team drifted into roadshows, business meetings, and deal-making, losing their core *jianghu* edge.
- **Tencent Investment and Self-Publishing:** Following mobile titles like *Phantom Blade 2* and *3* (which peaked at 150 million RMB in monthly revenue), S-GAME bought back their shares from investors, secured over 400 million RMB from Tencent for a ~20% stake, and ultimately chose to self-publish *Phantom Blade Zero* to maintain complete creative control.

## 4. Game Design, AI, and Industry Perspectives
- **Craft vs. Dao:** **Liang** humbly describes his team's work as possessing solid technical craft (*shu*), while acknowledging their inner cultivation (*dao*) still falls short of legendary industry creators.
- **The 99% Internal Rationale:** **Liang** asserts that external hot trends (like esports or anime styles in *Phantom Blade 2*) account for only 1% of success; 99% relies on the creator's internal rationale, lived experience, and genuine personality.
- **The Limits of AI in Single-Player Games:** While pro-AI for technical optimization, **Liang** emphasizes that AI cannot replace the brand premium and consumer trust built by human labor, painstaking artistry, and auteur-driven creation over decades.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Liang Qiwei** predicts that the era of relying on external industry tailwinds or quick market pivots is over for Chinese AAA games, forcing developers to rely entirely on authentic, original IP and deep internal cultivation.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Only in darkness can a meteor's light illuminate eternity."*
> — **Liang Qiwei** (quoting Gu Long)

> *"We know exactly what you are... It's hatred, vengeance, being wronged... So why are you suddenly serving me some bleeding-heart saint act?"*
> — **Liang Qiwei** (translating core player reactions to insincere narrative framing)

> *"The pursuit itself is the goal... You've attained advanced martial arts; what you pursue is even more advanced martial arts. There is no other purpose."*
> — **Liang Qiwei**
